subject: File control entry
notes: ALL FOUR SENTENCES OF GR3 MEASURED. (1) The TIMING lead - "The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1" - is FileRegistry.OpenCore's single Associate call, ahead of the Table-19 arbitration and OUTSIDE the RETRY loop (the content is read once per statement, not once per attempt); the SORT/MERGE implicit opens reach the same dispatch through CobolFile.OpenInput/OpenOutput. pb324_assign_using_dynamic moves two different names into data-name-1 and reads both files back through ONE connector, and its DELB=00 leg proves DELETE FILE acts on the association the last OPEN established rather than re-resolving. (2) GR3 a) - device-name-1/literal-1 "in the source unit that specifies the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement" - is the non-dynamic arm of FileConnector.Associate(spec, dynamic), which the emitter feeds with the EXECUTING unit's own ASSIGN target rather than with whatever was registered first. (3) GR3 b) - data-name-1 "in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement" - is the dynamic arm, and the two PB673 goldens are what discriminate it: pb673_external_assign_executor has TWO programs describing ONE external file connector (13.18.22.4 GR4 a), the second activating LAST and the first executing the OPEN, and pins that the record lands in the EXECUTOR's file (CHKB=05, CHKA=00, READA=AAAAA); pb673_recursive_assign_linage does the same across ACTIVATIONS of one RECURSIVE unit whose data-name-1 is in LOCAL-STORAGE (CHKI=05, CHKO=00). Before kb/Work PB673 both answered with the last INSTALLER's data item, silently, at status 00. (4) The closing sentence - the statement is unsuccessful when the association cannot be made - is 9.1.13.6 item 2's '31', pinned by pb324_assign_using_dynamic's BLANK=31 leg. The CONTENT rules that decide when it cannot be made are GR4's implementor determination, adjudicated on its own row (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-73 / DOC-A.1-10). EDITIONS, PER BRANCH (kb/Work PB746): GR3's lead sentence, a) and the closing sentence govern the ASSIGN TO clause at every edition; b) exists only where its phrase does, and the USING phrase is a COBOL-2002 introduction (kb/Work PB746): Annex E never names it, so it predates 2023, and GnuCOBOL 3.2's per-standard dialect files date it at 2002 (cobol85.conf assign-using-variable: unconformable; cobol2002.conf and cobol2014.conf: ok; cobc -std=cobol85 refuses `ASSIGN USING`) - constructs row assign-using-2002, VCR row 7.27; below 2002 the phrase is COBOL0900 on both arms (conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb746-assign-using-below-2002). b) rides conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb746_assign_using_2002 at its introducing edition. The sentence this replaces ('unchanged across 85/2002/2014/2023, and the 85 arm rides conformance:85/pb324_assign_using_85') was an inherited belief, and that golden had been written FROM it. retired-witness: conformance:85/pb324_assign_using_85 (moved to conformance:cases/12.4.5-File-control/pb746_assign_using_2002: the USING phrase is a 2002 introduction (kb/Work PB746), so the golden runs at its introducing edition)
